halt_reason: B05 halted at step 0, before the founder was asked to click anything, because Anthropic's session proxy sits in front of GitHub in a cloud session and refuses four things this build depends on (all [Certain - run], recorded route by route in docs/v2/build/probe/B05-environment-measurements.md). First, the lock: POST /git/commits, POST /git/refs, PATCH /git/refs and DELETE /git/refs are all refused, so lock.py's acquire() raises before any agent is dispatched and no unattended tick can run; worse, release() discards the API return code, so it reports 'Lock released.' on a lock that is still held - the exact state this spec calls worse than having no lock - and lock.py is outside this build's touches, so this build cannot fix it. Second, the attacks: POST /statuses/{sha} (A4), POST /rulesets (A6) and GET /collaborators (A12) are refused by the proxy, and no route deletes a branch (part of A5), so those four would be refused for the proxy's reason instead of GitHub's, which this spec says proves nothing - and A4, A5 and A6 are precisely the attacks BLUEPRINT 2.5 needs before its first two rows can stop being tripwires. Third, GET /actions/permissions is refused, so Deliver 2's two workflow-token settings cannot be read back through the API as Deliver 3 requires. Fourth, the fork: option (a) below sets one required approval on v2-build, which changes Deliver 3's ruleset and inverts A10's known answer from 'merges' to 'refused', so the 45 minutes of ruleset clicking cannot be spent until the option is chosen. Whether a session on the founder's Mac is behind the same proxy is untested and untestable from here; it decides between a cheap outcome and an expensive one, so it is the first question, not a side note.
halt_options: 0. ANSWER THIS FIRST, it may make the rest moot (2 minutes, on the Mac). In a Claude Code session on the Mac, run: gh api -X DELETE repos/vedantgautam1/chronos/git/refs/heads/lock/proxytest . If the branch disappears, the Mac is not proxied: B05 resumes there almost as written - the lock works, A4/A5/A6/A12 become runnable, and the only open question is Deliver 5's cloud scheduled task, which is tested separately by firing it once. If it answers 403 '... not permitted through this proxy.', the restriction is the platform's and options a-d below are the real decision.

a. The founder merges every build himself (the spec's own option (a)): one required approval on v2-build as well as main. A real wall for everything, one click per build, and the loop waits for him. Needs Deliver 3's v2-build ruleset built differently and A10's known answer inverted. Does NOT by itself fix the lock: the loop still needs the lock to serialise its own ticks, so this is an answer to the approval question only.

b. A reviewer with its own identity (the spec's own option (b)): a second automation account whose approval v2-build requires, or a reviewer from another AI family acting through its own GitHub app. Unattended, and a wall against self-approval. More setup, possibly a second subscription. Same caveat as (a): it does not fix the lock.

c. Proceed with guard rails, in writing (the spec's own option (c)), with the gate audit as the control: a bad build is found at the gate and the phase is redone from there. This is the only option that needs no new build work, and it is the honest label for what the five layers actually are today.

d. Correct the lock's backend in its own small build before B05 resumes. git push can create refs/heads/lock/<id> and can force-push it, and both are allowed from cloud; only delete is not, so release would have to become something other than a delete, and GitHubRefs.delete must stop discarding its return code. lock.py and loop_cli.py are founder-owned and outside B05's touches, so this is a new spec the founder approves, not something B05 can do. Cheapest route to an unattended loop IF option 0 says the Mac is proxied too; unnecessary if it says otherwise.

e. Split B05. Deliver 1-4 (identity, settings, rulesets, and the eight attacks that ARE runnable: A1, A2, A3, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11) do not need the lock and are worth having under every option above. Deliver 5-6 (the scheduled task and the three probes) wait on whichever of 0/a-d is chosen. This costs the founder ~45 minutes now instead of ~60 later and leaves A4, A5, A6 and A12 explicitly unproven in BLUEPRINT 2.5 rather than silently assumed. Recommended only if option 0 says the Mac is proxied; if it does not, do the whole build on the Mac instead and split nothing.

HOUSEKEEPING, needs the founder's own account either way: two branches created by the measurements in probe/B05-environment-measurements.md cannot be deleted from a cloud session - lock/proxytest and doc/b05-deltest, both pointing at v2-build's head b9c4f5d. Neither is on the ladder and neither affects a guard. Option 0's command deletes the first one as a side effect.
